model.heading: Model
model.notFound: No models found for this provider. The catalog might be empty or still loading.

providerHealth.heading: Provider Health
providerHealth.hint: Which provider/model pairs are healthy, degraded, or blocked — and why.
providerHealth.explain402: Billing limit reached (402). Blocked for ~15 minutes until quota resets.
providerHealth.explain403quota: Usage limit reached for this billing cycle. Blocked until the next cycle resets (~15 min).
providerHealth.explain403auth: Permission/auth error. Non-retryable — check your API key and access rights.
providerHealth.explain429: Rate limit hit (429). Temporary throttle — recovers automatically.
providerHealth.explain529: Server overloaded (529). The provider is under heavy load.
providerHealth.explainNetwork: Network unreachable. Check your internet or the provider's status page.
providerHealth.explainTimeout: Request timed out (408). The provider was slow to respond.
providerHealth.explainStreamHang: Stream stalled (599). The provider stopped mid-response.
providerHealth.explainQuota: Quota exhausted. Blocked until the reset window.

connection.wsUrlHint: URL of the agent WebSocket server. The server runs alongside the CLI.
connection.startingBody: For development, run ./dev.ps1 from the repo root (optionally set WS_HOST/WS_PORT first). Otherwise launch the WebUI with the CLI: wstack --webui.
connection.healthHint: Live ownership, storage, queue, watcher, and latency report for project services.
connection.healthRestartRequired: Restart the backend once to activate connection health reporting.
connection.endpointInvalidRemedy: The IPC socket path exceeds this platform's length limit, so the shared daemon cannot start. Queries fall back to a slower process-local mode. Remedy: set a shorter TMPDIR (e.g. export TMPDIR=/tmp) and restart WrongStack.
connection.restartAllTitle: Restart every running IPC daemon in one go
connection.versionSkewRemedy: This daemon is still running the release it was started on, not the installed one. Use Restart on this service (or Restart all) to load the current version.

agent.autonomyModeHint: How independently the agent proceeds between turns.
agent.autoProceedDelayHint: Milliseconds before the agent auto-proceeds in Auto mode. 0 = immediate.
agent.yoloHint: Run tool calls without asking — except the damaging kinds listed below.
agent.yoloPlusHint: Never ask — not even the damaging kinds or the two locked ones, and subagents may do the same. Your explicit deny rules still refuse.
agent.yoloConfirmIntro: YOLO runs everything else unattended. These are the kinds of damage it stops and asks you about first.
agent.yoloConfirmLockedNote: These two always ask. They write the files that decide whether you get asked at all, so turning them off would let the agent switch its own approval system off.

execution.maxIterationsHint: Maximum LLM turns per run. 0 = unlimited.
execution.autoProceedMaxIterationsHint: Stop auto-proceed after N iterations. 0 = unlimited.

features.chimeraModelHint: Model for the review agent. Requires a provider first.

features.autoReviewCascadeOnHint: When a review finds issues at or above this severity, spawn follow-up agents.

features.autoReviewModelSelectionHint: Choose the next profile model in order, or pick a random starting model for each review.

features.autoReviewModelHint: Model for the auto-review agent. Requires a provider first.

features.autoReviewPickModelHint: Select a provider and model, or a named fallback profile, for mid-session auto-review.
features.pluginsPerPluginHint: Enable or disable individual plugins. Changes take effect on next session.

fallbacks.heading: Fallback / Round-robin Models
fallbacks.body: These ordered model chains support failover and profile-based round-robin selection. On rate limits, 5xx errors, or stalls, the agent retries on the next available model.

fallbacks.favoritesOnlyHint: When auto fallback derives a chain, restrict it to your favorite models.
fallbacks.favoritesEmpty: Favorites are shown first and can constrain auto fallback.

fallbackSuggest.heading: Suggested fallback profiles
fallbackSuggest.body: Built from the models.dev catalog of the providers you have saved — current, tool-capable models only. Disabled models, deprecated models, superseded versions and anything more than six months behind the newest release are left out.
fallbackSuggest.llmHint: Your active model re-ranks the same catalog pool using what it knows about benchmarks and reliability. It can only pick models you can reach.
fallbackSuggest.empty: Not enough reachable models for a fallback chain. Add another provider or enable more models.
fallbackSuggest.poolSummary_one: Drawn from {{count}} model across your providers
fallbackSuggest.poolSummary_other: Drawn from {{count}} models across your providers

archetypeHint.balanced: Capable enough for real work at a sensible price.
archetypeHint.fast: Lowest latency that still drives tools reliably.
archetypeHint.budget: Cheapest models that can still finish coding tasks.

brain.heading: Brain
brain.headingHint: Decision models, council, escalation and risk ceiling — applied live, saved to the global config.
brain.escalationModeHint: Headless: the Brain never blocks on a human — unanswered escalations resolve via the safe terminal policy. Applies to CLI/TUI sessions; the standalone WebUI Brain is always headless.
brain.escalationDecisionTimeoutHint: Per-LLM-call time budget for one Brain decision.
brain.escalationHumanTimeoutHint: Interactive mode: how long an escalation prompt may wait before the terminal policy resolves it.
brain.escalationTerminalPolicyHint: How a headless escalation resolves with no human available. Conservative accepts a recommended option at low/medium risk; deny-all never auto-accepts; continue-on-recommended accepts a recommended option at ANY risk.
brain.escalationDecisionLogSizeHint: Rolling in-memory decision log kept for the status view.
brain.rulesBody: Evaluated before any provider call — first match wins. Edit them in the global config file; this view is read-only.
brain.heuristicsBody: Free pattern guesses that settle a question before any model runs. All on by default — turn one off when its guess is wrong for your workload.
brain.heuristicsLowRiskHint: Auto-answer low-risk requests that already carry a recommended option.
brain.heuristicsBlockedHint: 'blocked …' plus an explicit resolution marker in the context resolves to continue.
brain.heuristicsDeadlockHint: 'deadlock' plus failed work units in the context resolves to skip and continue.
brain.heuristicsRetryHint: 'failed'/'retry' plus demonstrably exhausted retries marks the unit failed and moves on.
brain.heuristicsPingHint: A bare continue/proceed ping with no competing alternative resolves to continue.
brain.qualityResponseBudgetHint: Output tokens per decision call. A Brain response is one decision plus a one-sentence rationale.
brain.qualityRejectHint: Treat a declined or empty response as 'this tier could not decide' instead of accepting it as an answer.
brain.qualityMinConfidenceHint: Reject answers whose self-reported confidence is below this. Responses reporting no confidence always pass.
brain.qualityDenyTerminalHint: Whether a deny from the single-LLM tier ends the decision. 'when-decided' makes a genuine refusal terminal while infrastructure failures still escalate.
brain.traceRecordHint: Per-decision JSONL of every tier, pool target and council vote, with timings and token usage. Off by default — enabling it writes decision content to disk.
brain.traceContentHint: 'full' keeps question and context (needed to replay a decision); 'redacted' truncates free text; 'none' records metadata only.
brain.cacheReplayHint: Reuse a previous council/LLM verdict for an identical repeated question. Deterministic tiers and ask-human are never cached; a decision the ledger observes to have failed is evicted.
brain.cacheLifetimeHint: How long a cached verdict stays replayable.
brain.monitorBody: Distress-signal self-activation. The monitor is built once at boot, so these apply to the next session rather than live.
brain.monitorWatchHint: Tool-failure streaks, error storms, agent stalls and file churn engage the Brain on their own.
brain.monitorPolicyHint: How a detected signal resolves. 'llm' consults the Brain; 'steer' always intervenes and 'observe' never does — both without a provider call.
brain.modelsUseSessionHint: Decide with whatever model the session is running. Turn off by adding models below.
brain.modelsPoolStrategyHint: Fallback: first model is primary, the rest are tried in order on failure. Round-robin: decisions rotate across the pool.
brain.councilEnableHint: High-stakes questions are voted on by independent seats (executor / skeptic-with-veto / auditor) instead of one model. Needs ≥2 resolvable voters (explicit seats below, or a ≥2-model pool).
brain.councilCustomLens: Custom decision lens — sent to the seat verbatim.
brain.councilRiskFloorHint: Minimum question risk that convenes the council instead of the single-model tier.
brain.councilJudgeDesc: Tie-breaker model that sees every vote's rationale.
brain.councilQuorumHint: Fraction of seats that must return a valid vote.
brain.councilApprovalHint: Fraction of cast vote weight the winning option must exceed.
brain.councilPerSeatTimeoutHint: Time budget for a single seat's vote. Slower than the decision timeout means one stalled seat holds up the vote.
brain.councilMaxConcurrencyHint: How many seats vote in parallel. Lower this when the pool shares one rate-limited provider.
brain.councilDistinctnessHint: Reject duplicate seats: 'model' requires distinct models, 'provider' requires independent providers so one outage cannot sway the vote.
brain.councilVoterBudgetHint: Output tokens per seat call — reasoning models spend thinking tokens from this budget.
brain.councilRoundsHint: Round 1 is independent. Later rounds show each seat the others’ ballots so it can revise. Only the last round is tallied — and every round costs one more call per seat.
brain.councilJudgeBudgetHint: Output tokens for the tie-breaking judge call.
brain.ledgerRecordHint: Persists every decision and its observed outcome; similar past outcomes are fed back into future Brain prompts.
brain.ledgerAutoDenyHint: Deny deterministically (no LLM) once this many consecutive approvals of a decision group ended in observed failures.
brain.ledgerMemoryEntriesHint: Ring size held in memory, and the number of past entries seeded from disk at boot.
brain.ledgerRetryWindowHint: A same-kind monitor intervention re-firing inside this window marks the previous steer as a failure.
brain.recentEmpty: No decisions recorded yet this session.
brain.pickPoolHint: Ordered decision pool — first is primary.
brain.pickVoterHint: Dialog stays open — add ≥2 voters, then close.
brain.persistError: Settings applied live but not saved.

jev.enabledHint: Off by default. Disabling stops all Jev requests, including tools and diagnostics, while keeping your key and feature choices.
jev.description: Manage the decision provider and see where Jev is used.
jev.timeout: No response from server. Reconnect and retry.
jev.routeChange: Changing provider clears the previous key, endpoint and model. Enter a new key or use the provider environment variable.
jev.keyHint: Leave blank to keep the current key
jev.removeKey: Remove saved key (environment key may still apply)
jev.featureHint: Switches permit Jev usage. Actual use also depends on the prerequisites and triggers below.
jev.testHint: The test sends one small billed request. Save changes first. Restart existing sessions to apply all consumers.
jev.activityHint: Refreshes every 3 seconds. Last 300 requests in this server process, across its sessions. No prompts, credentials or raw errors. Disk log rotates at 5 MB. Answered means a typed response, not necessarily a decision accepted by the consumer.
jev.empty: No matching Jev requests yet. Test the connection or use an enabled feature.
jev.readinessScope: These are saved profile conditions, not the live state of every session. A request below means the service was called, not that its answer was accepted.
jev.notObserved: No runtime request in the displayed recent log.
jev.contextScope: Selective enables the Jev selection path. Save changes and restart existing sessions; a session-specific strategy can override this profile setting.
jev.tiersHint: Enable tiers and define at least two levels, cheapest first. Set their models or fallback profiles and a default tier. Changes here save immediately.
jev.checkHint: Runs 22 synthetic cases across all 11 features using the saved account, including disabled features. Makes billed API calls, sends no project content and changes no feature settings. Passing does not prove workload quality or that a session uses the feature.

reasons.disabled: This feature is not permitted to use Jev.
reasons.account-required: Configure a valid Jev account first.
reasons.selective-required: Jev selection requires selective compaction; hybrid and intelligent do not use this selector.
reasons.tiers-disabled: The model tier system is disabled.
reasons.tiers-required: Define at least two model tiers.
reasons.skills-disabled: The global skills feature is disabled.
reasons.trigger-required: Runs only when its trigger conditions are met.
reasons.recall-injection-required: SAGE turn context recall is disabled; the Jev recall filter requires this path.

triggers.brain: Runs before later decision tiers; uncertain answers defer.
triggers.memoryTriage: Runs during triage value evaluation and merge decisions.
triggers.topicShift: Runs when topic-change prechecks require a judgment; repeated results may be cached.
triggers.memoryRecall: Filters candidates returned by SAGE turn context recall; cached judgments are reused.
triggers.compaction: Rates middle conversation turns during selective compaction; requires a provider and sufficient history.
triggers.kanbanVerify: Judges open agent-type criteria against changed files and their diff.
triggers.modelTier: Suggests a tier for delegations with no explicit model/tier and no matching role/phase route.
triggers.semanticLint: Runs when the semantic lint command finds candidates; it is not an automatic edit watcher.
triggers.tool: Runs when an agent calls the jev tool with evidence and typed questions.
triggers.skillSuggestion: Requires skills enabled, at least two skills, and gate/fit thresholds; results may be cached.
triggers.fleetDispatch: Runs only for ambiguous routing with multiple candidate roles.

jev.recallTurnHint: Adds relevant memories to each new turn; the Jev recall filter runs on this path. Memory and SAGE must also be enabled. Save and restart existing sessions.
jev.logContent: Record full request/response content in the log file
jev.logContentHint: Writes the state sent, the full question wording and the answers with their distributions to the Jev log file. This view stays metadata-only either way, and the account key is scrubbed. Turn it off when you are done. Save and restart existing sessions.
jev.logContentOn: Full request/response content is recorded in this file. It is never shown here.
jev.logContentOff: Metadata only. Full request/response content is not recorded.
